Chris Pappas

Democratic candidate for United States Senator, New Hampshire · Open seat

U.S. Representative for New Hampshire's 1st Congressional District; co-owner of his family's Puritan Backroom Restaurant in Manchester

Chris Pappas is a Democrat who has represented New Hampshire's 1st Congressional District in the U.S. House since 2019. Before that, he served on the New Hampshire Executive Council. He announced his run for the open seat of retiring Sen. Jeanne Shaheen on April 3, 2025, filed on June 8, 2026, and won the Democratic primary on September 8, 2026, with about 65% of the vote against Karishma Manzur.

Where Pappas stands

Cost of living / energy
Proposes suspending the federal gas tax and adding $1 billion to LIHEAP, the federal program that helps low-income households pay for home heating.
Housing
Supports federal funding for towns that reform local zoning to allow new housing, such as tiny homes and mixed-use development. Supports bipartisan legislation to limit Wall Street purchases of single-family homes.
Tariffs and trade
Calls for 'getting rid of these reckless tariffs.' Says they have raised costs for households and created uncertainty for small businesses.
Immigration and border security
Opposes abolishing ICE. Supports more border patrol resources and technology at checkpoints to stop fentanyl, and backs modernizing the immigration system.
Campaign finance
Supports reining in dark money and limiting the influence of Citizens United. Has made limiting big money in politics part of his Senate campaign.
Abortion
Opposes a federal abortion ban. Supports restoring Roe v. Wade protections nationally.
Social Security and Medicare
Opposes privatizing Social Security or means-testing its benefits. Supports strengthening Social Security and Medicare.
Federal deficit
Supports a bipartisan commission to identify ways to reduce the deficit. Says large corporations and the wealthy should pay their 'fair share.'
War powers / foreign policy
Said the military operation to capture Venezuela's Maduro should have had Congressional approval. Opposes U.S. involvement in open-ended nation-building.
Israel, Ukraine, Taiwan
Supports continued U.S. security assistance to Israel, Ukraine and Taiwan. Introduced legislation to speed delivery of resources to Taiwan.

Background

  • U.S. Representative, New Hampshire 1st District, 2019–present
  • Member, New Hampshire Executive Council (before 2019)
  • Co-owner, Puritan Backroom Restaurant, Manchester (family business)
  • Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate, won primary September 8, 2026
